## Computer control

Open apps, move the mouse, type, and run local shell commands.

| Command | What it does | Say it like this |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `open_application` | Launch an application by name on the local machine. | "Open Blender"<br>"Launch Notepad" |
| `mouse_and_keyboard` | Control mouse and keyboard: click, type, scroll, hotkeys. | "Click the Save button"<br>"Press Control plus S" |
| `capture_screen` | Take a compressed screenshot and return it as base64. | "Take a screenshot" |
| `run_terminal_command` | Run a shell command. Destructive commands require confirmation. | "Run dir in the terminal" |
| `manage_files` | Read, write, search, or remove local files. | "Copy report.docx into Documents" |
| `list_open_windows` | List all open application windows with their titles, which monitor each is on, and which one has focus. The summary is spoken aloud for blind/low-vision users. | "What windows are open?" |
| `focus_or_manage_window` | Manage an application window by name or title across Windows, macOS and Linux. Actions: focus, maximize, minimize, close, move_to_primary_monitor. | "Focus the Blender window"<br>"Minimize this window" |
| `set_active_monitor` | Switch the screen/vision capture target to a specific monitor. Use when the user says 'look at my second monitor' or asks to switch displays. Monitor numbers are 1-based. | "Use monitor two" |
| `type_text` | Type text into the field that currently has keyboard focus. Used for voice dictation; long passages are pasted from the local clipboard. | "Type hello world" |
| `select_all` | Select all text in the focused field. | "Select all" |
| `copy_selection` | Copy the current selection to the local clipboard. | "Copy the selection" |
| `paste_here` | Paste the clipboard at the caret. | "Paste here" |
| `delete_word` | Delete the word immediately left of the caret. | "Delete the last word" |
| `select_model` | Select a local model for chat or screen vision. Refuses models the detected RAM/VRAM cannot support. Use only after the user has chosen an available upgrade in Settings. | "Switch to wake-word mode"<br>"Use qwen3.5:9b for chat" |
| `undo_last_action` | Undo the last action: reverse a recent file move when reversible, otherwise send the active app's undo shortcut. | "Undo that" |

## Install software

Install an app with its native package manager, with confirmation.

| Command | What it does | Say it like this |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `install_application` | Install an application on the local machine using native silent package managers (winget/choco/brew/flatpak/snap/apt/dnf/pacman). Asks the user for confirmation before installing. Falls back to visually downloading from  | "Install Blender"<br>"Install VS Code" |

## Screen understanding

Describe the screen or carry out a multi-step goal through the visual agent.

| Command | What it does | Say it like this |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `describe_screen` | Describe what is currently on the screen ALOUD for a blind or low-vision user. Use when the user asks what's on screen, to read a dialog/error, or to find the focused control. Speaks the result. | "What's on my screen?"<br>"Read the dialog out loud" |
| `list_a11y_controls` | List named buttons, menus, dialogs and inputs from the OS accessibility tree. Prefer this over vision for standard controls. | "List the controls in this window" |
| `run_visual_task` | Execute a multi-step desktop GUI goal end to end: launch the app, perform each action in order, verify each step and recover from stalls. Use this whenever the user asks for several GUI actions in one request (for exampl | "Open Blender, create a new project, delete the default cube, and add a sphere"<br>"Open DaVinci Resolve and import the clips" |
| `stop_automation` | Immediately stop any running GUI/vision automation. Use when the user says stop, abort, cancel the task, or wants the agent to halt. | "Stop automation"<br>"Abort task"<br>"Emergency stop" |

## Web browsing

Read and interact with web pages using accessible names, not pixel coordinates.

| Command | What it does | Say it like this |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `open_url` | Open a website or search the web in the local browser. Pass a full URL (http/https) to visit it, or plain words to run a private web search (DuckDuckGo/Startpage, no API key). | "Open example.com" |
| `read_page_summary` | Read the active browser page as concise, spoken-friendly text: headings, main article text, form fields, and interactive buttons/links. Navigation bars and clutter are removed. Use this for reading articles, search resul | "Summarize this page" |
| `click_web_element` | Click a button, link, or control on the active web page by its visible text or ARIA label, with no pixel coordinates. | "Click the Log in button on this page" |
| `fill_web_field` | Type text into an input, textarea, or search field on the active web page, located by its label or placeholder. | "Fill the search field with quarterly report" |
| `list_landmarks_and_headings` | Read the semantic structure of the active web page: HTML landmarks (main, navigation, article, form, aside) and the H1-H3 heading hierarchy. Use for 'jump to main content', 'skip navigation', 'read the headings on this p | "List the headings on this page" |
| `read_web_table` | Read an HTML data table row by row with each column header paired to its cell, instead of dumping raw text. Use when the user asks to read a table, a schedule, prices, or comparison data on the page. table_index is zero  | "Read the prices table" |
| `list_actionable_links` | List numbered, meaningful links and buttons on the active page, skipping empty or decorative icon controls. Use for 'what links are here', 'list the buttons', 'open link 3' or 'find a link about X'. Then click it with cl | "What links can I click here?" |

## Files and clipboard

Find, read, organize, and copy local files and text.

| Command | What it does | Say it like this |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `read_clipboard` | Read the user's local clipboard text. Use when they ask what they just copied or to summarize/act on clipboard contents. | "What's copied?" |
| `write_clipboard` | Copy a result or text to the local clipboard. | "Copy that result to my clipboard" |
| `inspect_recent_files` | List recently modified files in Downloads/Desktop/Documents or an explicit local directory, with sizes, types and ages. Use for 'what did I just download' or 'open the PDF I just downloaded'. | "What did I download recently?" |
| `read_back_last_dictation` | Speak dictated text back verbatim so the user can check accuracy. | "Read back what I just dictated" |
| `find_files` | Find local files by name in Home/Downloads/Desktop/Documents or an explicit folder. Returns names, folders and modified dates and speaks the summary. Use for 'where is my passport scan'. | "Find my budget spreadsheet" |
| `read_document_aloud` | Read a local .txt, .md, .pdf or .docx document aloud (or a matching section) for blind/low-vision users. | "Read this PDF aloud" |
| `organize_files` | Move, copy or rename local files into a destination folder. Overwrites require spoken confirmation. Never deletes files. | "Move these screenshots into a folder" |

## Settings and models

Change speech, listening, and local model choices by voice.

| Command | What it does | Say it like this |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `get_settings` | Read the current Murmur AI preferences. | "Show current settings" |
| `set_setting` | Change one or more Murmur AI preference values. | "Increase mic threshold"<br>"Turn chimes off" |
| `list_model_upgrades` | List optional better local models this device can actually run, with their hardware requirements. Current models remain the default. | "Show available model upgrades" |
| `add_pronunciation` | Teach Murmur how to pronounce a word or acronym. Use when the user says 'pronounce NVDA as N-V-D-A'. | "Pronounce GUI as gooey" |
| `set_voice_profile` | Switch between named voice profiles (default, clear, fast, quiet, natural) that set speech rate, voice, chimes and verbosity. 'natural' uses the clearest fully-local voice. | "Switch to the clear voice profile" |
| `start_demo` | Start a guided, eyes-free practice walkthrough with four safe tasks. It never modifies files or settings. | "Start the tutorial" |

## Diagnostics and updates

Check health, export a privacy-safe diagnostics bundle, and install updates.

| Command | What it does | Say it like this |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `run_diagnostics` | Check the microphone, Ollama, local models, OS permissions and display session, then speak a plain-English status report. Use when the user asks why Murmur AI is not working or to run diagnostics. | "Run diagnostics"<br>"Why aren't you working?" |
| `export_diagnostics` | Create a privacy-safe local diagnostics zip (logs, hardware profile, Ollama status and sanitized config) and speak its exact path. Use when the user wants to report a bug or attach a log. | "Export a diagnostics bundle" |

## Privacy, secrets, and memory

Store secrets locally and control what Murmur remembers.

| Command | What it does | Say it like this |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `set_secret_reference` | Store an optional provider key or MCP token in the OS keychain (or the encrypted local vault when no keychain daemon exists). The value is hidden: never repeat it aloud or in a summary. Confirm only that the named secret | "Remember my API key as OPENAI_API_KEY" |
| `list_configured_secrets` | List which secret references are configured or missing. Reports names and status only; never reads or speaks secret values. | "Which secrets are configured?" |
| `delete_secret` | Delete a named secret from the keychain. Requires an explicit confirm=true argument after the user confirms; never speaks or returns the deleted value. | "Delete my stored API key" |
| `remember_fact` | Remember a non-private fact about the user. Refuses passwords, keys, emails, card numbers and phone numbers. | "Remember that my project is called Orca" |
| `list_memories` | Speak everything Murmur remembers about the user. | "What do you remember about me?" |
| `forget_memory` | Forget one remembered fact by id, undoable until the next action. | "Forget that fact" |
| `undo_forget` | Restore the last fact that was forgotten. | "Undo that forget" |

## Plugins, recipes, and skills

Manage local MCP plugins, lookup recipes, and app skill packs.

| Command | What it does | Say it like this |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list_mcp_tools` | List the active MCP/plugin servers and the tools they expose. Use when the user asks what plugins or MCP tools are active. | "What plugins are active?" |
| `reload_mcp_plugins` | Reload ~/.murmur-ai/mcp_servers.json and reconnect to all MCP servers. Use when the user says reload my plugins. | "Reload my plugins" |
| `list_tool_recipes` | List reviewed local look-up tools the user has enabled. | "List my tool recipes" |
| `run_tool_recipe` | Run an enabled local look-up tool with one text input. | "Run the lookup recipe" |
| `list_skill_packs` | List available declarative app workflow packs and their shortcuts. | "Which app skills are available?" |

## Voice settings

These phrases are matched locally before the model is called, so they work
even when Ollama is offline.

| Area | Say it like this |
| --- | --- |
| Speech | "Speak faster", "Use the natural voice", "Switch to the clear voice profile" |
| Sounds | "Turn chimes off", "Be quiet", "Turn spatial audio cues off" |
| Listening | "Switch to wake-word mode", "Increase mic threshold", "Mute the microphone" |
| Screen descriptions | "Switch to detailed screen descriptions", "Screen reader friendly on" |
| Privacy | "Keep my data when I uninstall", "Clear my data when I uninstall" |
| Start-up | "Start Murmur when I log in", "Disable startup launch" |
| Models | "Show current models", "Preview plans on", "Start the tutorial" |
| Pronunciation | "Pronounce GUI as gooey" |

## Built-in skill packs

Skill packs carry hotkeys and terminology only. They never contain executable code.

### Blender (`blender`)

Blender is a custom 3D canvas. Use SoM grounding for the viewport and the a11y tree for menus and panels. Prefer shortcuts for transforms.

| Action | Shortcut |
| --- | --- |
| deselect | `alt+a` |
| move | `g` |
| object mode | `tab` |
| rotate | `r` |
| scale | `s` |
| select all | `a` |
| undo | `ctrl+z` |

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| outliner | the panel listing scene objects |
| properties | the panel with object settings |
| timeline | the frame strip at the bottom |
| viewport | the main 3D canvas area |

### DaVinci Resolve (`davinci_resolve`)

DaVinci Resolve timelines are custom canvases. Use SoM grounding for the timeline and viewer; use the a11y tree for menus and dialogs.

| Action | Shortcut |
| --- | --- |
| fit timeline | `shift+z` |
| mark in | `i` |
| mark out | `o` |
| play pause | `space` |
| split clip | `s` |
| undo | `ctrl+z` |

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| inspector | the panel with clip settings |
| media pool | the area holding imported clips |
| timeline | the clip strip where edits happen |
| viewer | the picture preview |

### Visual Studio Code (`vscode`)

VS Code is mostly standard controls. Prefer the accessibility tree and keyboard shortcuts over vision.

| Action | Shortcut |
| --- | --- |
| command palette | `ctrl+shift+p` |
| find | `ctrl+f` |
| go to line | `ctrl+g` |
| quick open | `ctrl+p` |
| save | `ctrl+s` |
| terminal | `ctrl+`` |

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| command palette | the quick-action menu |
| editor | the text area |
| explorer | the file tree panel |

## Configuration defaults

Preferences live in `~/.murmur-ai/config.json`. Launch-at-login is opt-in,
and the OS registration is the source of truth.

| Setting | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `autostart_enabled` | `false` |
| `chat_model` | `""` |
| `clear_data_on_uninstall` | `false` |
| `description_verbosity` | `"concise"` |
| `earcons` | `true` |
| `echo_guard` | `true` |
| `echo_guard_tail_ms` | `250` |
| `listening_mode` | `"active"` |
| `loopback_guard` | `false` |
| `media_ducking` | `false` |
| `mic_threshold` | `0.5` |
| `preview_plans` | `false` |
| `provider` | `""` |
| `remote_companion_enabled` | `false` |
| `screen_reader_friendly` | `false` |
| `spatial_audio_cues` | `true` |
| `speech_rate` | `1.0` |
| `vision_model` | `""` |
| `voice` | `"af_heart"` |
| `voice_profile` | `"default"` |

## Keeping this reference current

Run `python scripts/generate_docs.py` after changing a tool schema, skill pack,
pronunciation, or setting default. `scripts/verify-all.ps1` and `verify-all.sh`
run `python scripts/generate_docs.py --check`, which fails if these files are stale.
The same generated data feeds the website's command and skill explorer.
